purpose: Validate the Phase 2 experimental procedure end-to-end on one (file, task) pair before running the full 9-file x 6-task experiment. No model has been called yet.

engine.note: Engine was not modified to produce this pilot - no new detection rules, no code changes. Both conditions below are direct, unedited engine output/input.

source_file.why_selected: Smallest suitable Java candidate with real code structure (a class, two methods, both field-adjacent and local-variable secrets) rather than a flat script. Contains three single-line detected values (api_key, password, client_secret categories in ground truth) plus one multiline Java '+'-concatenated value, exercising both the ordinary and multiline placeholder paths in one small (24-line) file. Matches the task's explicit preference for a small Java example with useful surrounding code structure.

original_condition.produced_by: Verbatim copy of benchmark/dataset/files/java/Config.java - the literal, unmodified developer source, never passed through the engine. This is the 'original' condition compared against in the AI evaluation (per ai-evaluation/README.md's methodology), distinct from the engine's own MASK-mode output.

sanitized_condition.produced_by: engine.scan_project(input_dir, output_dir, rules, placeholder_mode=True) run against an isolated single-file copy of the dataset directory. File content copied verbatim from the engine's actual output directory - not hand-authored or hand-edited.

placeholders_generated.note: first fragment of a 3-fragment '+'-concatenation; fragments on lines 20-21 are emptied, not separately tokenized

sanitized_condition.category_resolution_note: apiKey and clientSecret resolve to GENERIC_SECRET rather than the more descriptive API_KEY. This is not a bug introduced for this pilot - it's the code-identifier code path's suspicious-keyword regex backtracking onto the generic 'key' alternative before the more specific 'apikey' one for these particular identifiers (a new, concrete instance of the category-resolution limitation already documented in BENCHMARK.md's Limitations section for the config-key vs value-pattern divergence). Detection, redaction, correlation, and distinctness are all still fully correct - apiKey and clientSecret correctly get two DIFFERENT tokens (GENERIC_SECRET_1 vs GENERIC_SECRET_2) since they are two different real values. Only the category LABEL is less specific than ideal. Flagged here because it's directly relevant to the research question: the AI sees '<GENERIC_SECRET_1>' where a human would say 'this is an API key' - worth watching for in the rubric's 'misunderstood a sanitized value' dimension.

verification.expected_detected_values_matched_ground_: benchmark/dataset/cases.jsonl case ids java_004_api_key, java_005_db_password, java_006_client_secret, java_007/008/009_multiline_frag1/2/3, all expected_detection=true at the documented lines - matched exactly.
verification.leak_check_method: For each placeholder-mode finding, confirmed entry['before'] (the raw fake secret text) does not occur anywhere in the sanitized file text.

syntax_check.method: benchmark/syntax_check.py check_syntax('.java', text) - heuristic bracket/quote-balance check (Java has no stdlib parser available to this project, per BENCHMARK.md's documented limitation)

verification.determinism_check: placeholder_mode=True scan run twice on the same isolated input copy; sanitized output byte-for-byte identical across both runs.

evaluation_task.why_this_prompt: Explicitly recommended by the task brief for the first pilot - least dependent on whether the file contains an actual bug (unlike identify_bug.md), so it exercises basic comprehension rather than a task the file may not be well-suited for.

template_variables.SOURCE_CODE: Filled with original/java/Config.java content verbatim for the original-condition call, and sanitized/java/Config.java content verbatim for the sanitized-condition call. No file path is included in the prompt (per prompts/README.md rule 5) - only the bare content, exactly as the template specifies.

model_to_be_evaluated.status: NOT YET SELECTED - no model has been called, no response has been generated, no result exists

settings_to_fix_at_run_time.conversation_history: none - each (file, task, condition) call is a single independent request
settings_to_fix_at_run_time.sampling: one call per condition for the pilot, no repeated sampling

experimental_controls.note: Per ai-evaluation/README.md 'Experimental controls' and prompts/README.md - the two conditions below differ ONLY in source representation.
held_identical_across_conditions: evaluation procedure (same rubric, same rater, blind where practical)
experimental_controls.only_variable: presence vs. absence of sanitization (original/java/Config.java vs sanitized/java/Config.java)
experimental_controls.condition_leakage_check: Neither file's content nor the prompt template contains the words sanitized/redacted/scrubbed/anonymized/masked/placeholder/fake/synthetic/benchmark (prompts/README.md rule 1) - verified: the source files themselves DO contain a 'fake-'-prefixed value and a 'Synthetic benchmark fixture' header comment, inherited from the dataset fixture design, present identically in both conditions, not introduced by sanitization - documented as a pre-existing pilot-file caveat below.

known_caveats_for_this_pilot_file: The source file's own header comment ('Synthetic benchmark fixture - every value below is fake...') and the literal 'fake-' prefix on each secret value are present in BOTH conditions (original and sanitized) since they predate this pilot and are part of the benchmark dataset's own synthetic-value labeling convention, not sanitization output. They are not a condition leak between original vs. sanitized (both conditions carry the same text), but they do mean this specific file is not representative of how a real, unlabeled codebase would read to a model - a genuine developer file would not announce 'this is fake' in a comment. Worth choosing a less self-describing file, or noting this caveat when interpreting results, for the full 9-file experiment.
See sanitized_condition.category_resolution_note above for the GENERIC_SECRET-vs-API_KEY category-label imprecision observed on this specific file.
